questions.question: What sign relation does Onsager reciprocity imply for the anomalous Hall conductivity when the magnetic order parameter is reversed?
questions.rationale: Combining Onsager reciprocity with σαβ=−σβα makes the Hall conductivity odd under L reversal.

questions.question: In the m′m2′ example, which field can induce Mz, and why can no single-axis field induce Mx?

options.A: Ey induces Mz by breaking my and 2′z; every single-axis field preserves at least one of m′x or my that forbids Mx
options.B: Ex induces Mz by breaking m′x; Ez alone induces Mx
options.C: Only [Ex,Ey] induces Mz, while Ey alone induces Mx
options.D: Any uniaxial field induces both because m′m2′ has no mirrors

questions.rationale: The example tracks how fields transform under the MPG operations and which forbidden magnetization components become allowed.
questions.evidence_quote: Applying a uni-axial electric field Ey naturally breaks my and 2′z symmetries

questions.question: Why are the 32 type-II magnetic point groups omitted from the electric-field-induced magnetization analysis?

options.A: They contain time-reversal as an independent symmetry, which forbids magnetization and is not broken by electric field
options.B: They contain no spatial operations, so Hall conductivity is undefined
options.C: They allow only nonlinear responses of fifth order or higher
options.D: They are all metallic and therefore excluded from first-principles calculations

questions.rationale: The field does not break time reversal, so these groups cannot host the magnetization underlying the AHE.

options.B: CoF₂ (̅3′m′) has only first-order uniaxial responses
options.C: CoF₂ has third-order responses only and requires all three field axes
options.D: CoF₂ has spontaneous Hall response and no field-driven terms

questions.question: What special field-orientation caveat do the authors note for fourth-order σyx in the 4mm.1 MPG?

options.A: The response is proportional to ExEy(E²x−E²y), so it is quenched when |Ex|=|Ey|
options.B: It is proportional to ExEy(E²x+E²y), so it vanishes only when one field is zero
options.C: It requires Ez and is independent of the relative Ex and Ey magnitudes
options.D: It is odd under swapping Ex and Ey and doubles when their magnitudes match

questions.rationale: The quartic effective-field term cancels for equal-magnitude in-plane field components.
questions.evidence_quote: When |Ex| = |Ey|, Bz eff = λzxxxyExEy(E2x −E2y) becomes zero
